cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Use the Proper Title
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your standing through a title, privilege, courtesy, or public sign of respect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. At the staff barbecue, introduce me as Director Patel. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm introducing everyone by first name. Even the owner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Then give me a separate introduction when I welcome the staff.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The owner's doing the welcome. You offered to serve burgers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then introduce the burger service: 'Director Patel will serve you.' I'd like them to hear who's making this gesture.

mechanism: A confidently manages a barbecue appearance but gives up speaking slots and accepts service duties to secure one public use of A director title.
confusable: Unlike demanding an apology, A wants a sign of current standing; authority depends on accommodating the introducer schedule and actual role.
comparison: Staff burger service and public introduction differ from a table name card and space-constrained title display.
seedUse: Use D57-a first names/owner welcome/burgers and S02-a claiming a revised arrangement as the chosen plan.
